messages:
mia: Heads-up — after last night's control-plane upgrade to 1.27 a subset of GPU nodepools in us-west-2 aren't scaling up. Pods queue, CA doesn't add nodes. Noticed it ~10m after the rollout.
sam: Seen that too. CA events look like it's not mapping nodes back to ASGs. Example from CA logs: `Ignored node providerID '' (failed to parse)`
chen: That sounds like providerID parsing. Any chance kubelet restarted with a new providerID format? We had a kubelet flag change in the kubelet release notes for 1.27.
mia: Yes. On one affected node `kubectl get node ip-10-0-3-42 -o yaml` shows providerID: `i-0abcd1234` (no aws:///us-west-2/ prefix). Other nodes still have `aws:///us-west-2/i-0abcd1234`.
ops-bot: [incident] 1769801111: autoscaler: scale-up prevented — providerID mismatch detected. Tags: gpu-pool, us-west-2
alex: CA relies on providerID to map nodes -> ASG in the cloud provider library. If providerID lost the scheme/zone prefix CA can't find the nodegroup and so won't scale.
raul: Any idea what change produced the short providerID? kubelet providerID formatting is normally set by the cloud provider code. Could be the in-tree removal or a kubelet arg.
jen: Quick repro: ssh to node, run `cat /proc/cmdline` to see kubelet flags, but we don't control kubelet flags on managed nodes. For our EKS managed nodepools this came from the node bootstrap.
sam: Short-term mitigation: we can patch cluster-autoscaler deployment to be tolerant — accept bare instance IDs by matching `i-[0-9a-f]+` and reconstruct providerID with region from node label `topology.kubernetes.io/region`. I sketched a small change in CA to normalize IDs.
mia: Can you paste the snippet?
sam: Sure:

```
// normalize providerID
if strings.HasPrefix(providerID, "i-") {
  region := node.Labels["topology.kubernetes.io/region"]
  providerID = fmt.Sprintf("aws:///%s/%s", region, providerID)
}
```

chen: That should be safe as a hotfix. We should also check why kubelet lost the prefix — if other clusters get upgraded they'll break too.
raul: +1 on a two-pronged approach: hotfix CA for immediate restore, and root-cause investigate with node bootstrap images.
ops-bot: [action] create PR for CA hotfix and schedule canary rollout to staging.
jen: For rollback plan: if CA hotfix causes issues we can pin CA image to previous tag and roll back within 5 min. Have the old image tag ready.
alex: Also file an infra ticket to audit the kubelet/node bootstrap changes in the 1.27 upgrade job; maybe a change in cloud-provider config or kubelet release stripped providerID parts.
mia: I'm going to: 1) open the CA hotfix PR (sam's snippet), 2) kick a canary in staging, 3) if green roll to prod GPUs only. ETA 30m for PR.
sam: PR created: https://git.internal/r/autoscaler/merge/542 — includes unit tests for providerID normalization.
chen: Running canary on staging now — monitoring will be in the autoscaler dashboard.
raul: Also pinged EKS team to check node bootstrap templates.
mia: Thanks. Keep updates here. If we don't have a hotfix in 45m we'll plan to rollback the control-plane upgrade for affected clusters.
ops-bot: [update] 1769802300: canary passed for normalized CA image on staging. No regressions in 15m.
jen: Scheduling prod canary for gpu-pool (3 nodes) at +10m.
ops-bot: [update] 1769803050: prod canary success. CA resumed scaling for gpu-pool in us-west-2. Rolling out to remaining GPU pools now.
raul: Follow-up ticket: INFRA-1294 — track kubelet/providerID regression + upgrade gating.
mia: Closing the thread after rollout complete. Thanks everyone :tada:
